notes:
Summary: Enterprise evaluation for Redwood Dedicated to replace an aging on-prem Triton fleet. Primary driver = predictable latency and cost for two distinct workloads: (1) real-time assembly_line_assistant (chat + small context retrieval) requiring p95 latency <200ms and hot KV/cache for operator prompts, and (2) nightly reranking + visual_inspection batch jobs that need high throughput (aggregate token throughput >10M tokens/hour).

Key technical asks (from SE call 2026-02-18):
- Throughput guarantees: want committed baseline for 1000 chat sessions (concurrent), with burst buffer to 3x for peak shift changes.
- Latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 targets: 50ms / 180ms / 400ms (short prompts, <=512 tokens). Must support p95 <200ms for operator-facing flows.
- Reserved GPU planning: proposal requested for mixed pool: 4x H100 (low-latency chat) + 8x A10/A100 class for embeddings/rerank batch. Customer asked for cost delta vs all-H100.
- SLA negotiations: target 99.95% uptime for control-plane + 99.9% for serving; wants service credits and a dedicated escalation path (phone) for Critical incidents.
- Model-specific tuning: intend to serve two model families: a 32k-context base LLaMA-derivative for deep-reasoning assist, and a compact 8k LLM tuned for short operator prompts. Requests: context-length tuning, recommended quantization profiles (int8 dynamic vs 4-bit quant), and per-model batching/KV cache presets.

POC scope and success metrics:
- Day 1: ingest internal model (on-prem variant) and run 3 canonical prompts (assembly instruction assist) to measure cold vs warm KV cache p95 latency.
- Day 2: run sustained synthetic traffic to validate throughput at 1000 concurrent sessions + 3x burst for 30m and measure tail latencies and token cost.
- Acceptance: p95 <200ms for short prompts, sustained batch throughput >=10M tokens/hour with <10% variance, automated fallback correctly routes to lower-cost pool <2% failed requests.

Engineering notes / config preferences:
- Quantization: prefer testing 8-bit dynamic first (maintain quality) then aggressive 4-bit quant for embeddings-only models. Need Redwood's recommended quant profile per model (including perf delta table).
- Context length: plan to cap operator prompts at 8k for chat pool, enable 32k on H100 pool for long-form diagnostics. Ask for memory footprint estimates per profile.
- Batching & KV cache: want continuous batching enabled for batch jobs and minimal batching for chat (target single-request latency). KV cache persistence across requests for same operator session is critical — ask about eviction policies and warmup times.
- Autoscaling policy: want predictable reserved capacity + burst autoscale to protect latency SLOs; prefer manual control during POC to observe behavior.

Security / compliance touches:
- Legal requested SOC2 Type II report and encryption at rest details (KMS/HSM).
- Data residency: manufacturing telemetry must remain in US region; private control plane acceptable.
- Pen test: internal sec team will run network/ingress test week of 2026-03-22.
